_comment: The float-bridge axioms tools/float_bridge/measure.py measures, how it reads each, and what it measured. Hand-authored except `pinned`, which `--record` writes. The harness fails if this and AXIOM_MANIFEST.md disagree about which axioms are float-bridge, if a `statement` is not the Lean source's, or if a measurement moves from its pin.

Certcom.floatOfR.reason: rounds a real to a Float: a function symbol. real_round_bounds reads it as IEEE round-to-nearest-even, as its docstring says

Certcom.realToR.reason: the real value a Float denotes: a function symbol, not a proposition. Every row here reads it as the exact value of a finite double; a non-finite float has none

Certcom.real_abs_eps.reason: an opaque constant with nothing stated about it; real_abs_rounds is what is measured

Certcom.real_abs_rounds.statement: : ∀ a : Float, a.isFinite = true → abs (realToR (stdI1 leanPrims .abs a) - abs (realToR a)) ≤ real_abs_eps

Certcom.real_acos_rounds.statement: : ∀ (R : MachLib.Real) (a : Float), a.isFinite = true → R < 1 → abs (realToR a) ≤ R → abs (realToR (stdI1 leanPrims .acos a) - arccos (realToR a)) ≤ u * pi

Certcom.real_asin_rounds.statement: : ∀ (R : MachLib.Real) (a : Float), a.isFinite = true → R < 1 → abs (realToR a) ≤ R → abs (realToR (stdI1 leanPrims .asin a) - arcsin (realToR a)) ≤ u * (pi / (1 + 1))

Certcom.real_atan_eps.reason: an opaque constant with nothing stated about it; real_atan_rounds is what is measured

Certcom.real_atan_rounds.statement: : ∀ a : Float, a.isFinite = true → abs (realToR (stdI1 leanPrims .atan a) - atan (realToR a)) ≤ real_atan_eps

Certcom.real_cos_eps.reason: an opaque constant with nothing stated about it; real_cos_rounds is what is measured

Certcom.real_cos_rounds.statement: : ∀ a : Float, a.isFinite = true → abs (realToR (stdI1 leanPrims .cos a) - cos (realToR a)) ≤ real_cos_eps

Certcom.real_cosh_finite.statement: : ∀ a : Float, a.isFinite = true → abs (realToR a) ≤ natCast 710 → (stdI1 leanPrims .cosh a).isFinite = true

Certcom.real_cosh_rounds.statement: : ∀ (R : MachLib.Real) (a : Float), (stdI1 leanPrims .cosh a).isFinite = true → abs (realToR a) ≤ R → abs (realToR (stdI1 leanPrims .cosh a) - cosh (realToR a)) ≤ (u + u + u + u) * cosh R

Certcom.real_exp_finite.statement: : ∀ a : Float, a.isFinite = true → realToR a ≤ natCast 709 → (stdI1 leanPrims .exp a).isFinite = true

Certcom.real_exp_rounds.statement: : ∀ (hi : MachLib.Real) (a : Float), a.isFinite = true → (stdI1 leanPrims .exp a).isFinite = true → dblMin ≤ exp (realToR a) → realToR a ≤ hi → abs (realToR (stdI1 leanPrims .exp a) - exp (realToR a)) ≤ (u + u) * exp hi

Certcom.real_log10_rounds.statement: : ∀ (lo hi : MachLib.Real) (a : Float), a.isFinite = true → 0 < lo → lo ≤ realToR a → realToR a ≤ hi → abs (realToR (stdI1 leanPrims .log10 a) - log10 (realToR a)) ≤ (u + u + u) * (abs (log10 lo) + abs (log10 hi))

Certcom.real_log_finite.statement: : ∀ a : Float, a.isFinite = true → 0 < realToR a → (stdI1 leanPrims .ln a).isFinite = true

Certcom.real_log_rounds.statement: : ∀ (lo hi : MachLib.Real) (a : Float), a.isFinite = true → 0 < lo → lo ≤ realToR a → realToR a ≤ hi → abs (realToR (stdI1 leanPrims .ln a) - log (realToR a)) ≤ (u + u) * (abs (log lo) + abs (log hi))

Certcom.real_round_bounds.statement: : ∀ M x : Real, 0 ≤ M → M ≤ dblMax → abs x ≤ M → (x = 0 ∨ dblMin ≤ abs x) → abs (realToR (floatOfR x) - x) ≤ u * M

Certcom.real_round_finite.statement: : ∀ x : Real, abs x ≤ dblMax → (floatOfR x).isFinite = true

Certcom.real_sin_eps.reason: an opaque constant with nothing stated about it; real_sin_rounds is what is measured

Certcom.real_sin_rounds.statement: : ∀ a : Float, a.isFinite = true → abs (realToR (stdI1 leanPrims .sin a) - sin (realToR a)) ≤ real_sin_eps

Certcom.real_sinh_finite.statement: : ∀ a : Float, a.isFinite = true → abs (realToR a) ≤ natCast 710 → (stdI1 leanPrims .sinh a).isFinite = true

Certcom.real_sinh_rounds.statement: : ∀ (R : MachLib.Real) (a : Float), (stdI1 leanPrims .sinh a).isFinite = true → abs (realToR a) ≤ R → abs (realToR (stdI1 leanPrims .sinh a) - sinh (realToR a)) ≤ (u + u + u + u) * cosh R

Certcom.real_sqrt_rounds.statement: : ∀ (hi : MachLib.Real) (a : Float), a.isFinite = true → 0 ≤ realToR a → realToR a ≤ hi → abs (realToR (stdI1 leanPrims .sqrt a) - sqrt (realToR a)) ≤ u * sqrt hi

Certcom.real_tan_rounds.statement: : ∀ (R : MachLib.Real) (a : Float), a.isFinite = true → 0 ≤ R → R < pi / (1 + 1) → abs (realToR a) ≤ R → abs (realToR (stdI1 leanPrims .tan a) - tan (realToR a)) ≤ (u + u) * tan R

Certcom.real_tanh_rounds.statement: : ∀ (a : Float), a.isFinite = true → abs (realToR (stdI1 leanPrims .tanh a) - tanh (realToR a)) ≤ u + u

tanh-at-1u.why: real_tanh_rounds as stated until 2026-09-14, with bound u; measured false

sqrt-at-quarter-u.why: sqrt is correctly rounded, so its error reaches about half an ulp, near u relative; a quarter of u must be exceeded

exp-as-stated-until-2026-09-14.why: real_exp_rounds as stated until 2026-09-14, restated that day from this measurement; kept so the run keeps showing it fails (subnormal results, and results just above a power of two)

exp-at-u-on-its-restated-domain.why: real_exp_rounds's 2026-09-14 hypotheses with its old constant u: glibc misrounds some results just above a power of two, so u fails even with subnormal and overflowing results excluded

sinh-as-stated-until-2026-09-14.why: real_sinh_rounds as stated until 2026-09-14, restated that day from this measurement; kept so the run keeps showing it fails

cosh-as-stated-until-2026-09-14.why: real_cosh_rounds as stated until 2026-09-14, restated that day from this measurement; kept so the run keeps showing it fails

log10-as-stated-until-2026-09-14.why: real_log10_rounds as stated until 2026-09-14, restated that day from this measurement; kept so the run keeps showing it fails

tan-as-stated-until-2026-09-14.why: real_tan_rounds as stated until 2026-09-14, restated that day from this measurement; kept so the run keeps showing it fails

fpbridge-as-stated-until-2026-09-14.why: real_fpbridge : FPBridge realToR as stated until 2026-09-14, restated that day from this measurement; kept so the run keeps showing it fails (products below DBL_MIN)

round-bounds-as-stated-until-2026-09-14.why: real_round_bounds as stated until 2026-09-14, restated that day from this measurement; kept so the run keeps showing it fails (reals below DBL_MIN)

fpfinite-tie-inclusive.why: real_fpfinite with its range widened to |exact result| <= DBL_MAX + 2^970: round-to-nearest-even rounds that tie up to infinity, so this must fail at the tie and nowhere else

fpfinite-no-range.why: real_fpfinite with no range at all: finite operands overflow

round-finite-tie-inclusive.why: real_round_finite with its range widened to |x| <= DBL_MAX + 2^970: the tie rounds up to infinity, so this must fail at the tie and nowhere else

round-finite-no-range.why: real_round_finite with no range at all: a real far above DBL_MAX overflows

literal-every-decimal.why: every decimal literal is floatOfR of its decimal, the generic statement the literal axioms deliberately do not make: Lean's Float.ofScientific truncates to 64 bits before rounding once, so a decimal within 2^-11 ulp above a binary64 midpoint rounds down to even

literal-0.05109.why: a four-digit decimal literal Lean evaluates to 0x3faa2877ee4e26d4 where round-to-nearest-even gives 0x3faa2877ee4e26d5: the literal check must see a one-ulp difference

exp-finite-at-710.why: real_exp_finite with its bound widened to 710: glibc's exp overflows above 709.782712893384, so this must fail, and only above 709

sinh-finite-at-711.why: real_sinh_finite with its bound widened to 711: the runtime sinh overflows above 710.4758600739439 in magnitude, so this must fail, and only above 710

cosh-finite-at-711.why: real_cosh_finite with its bound widened to 711: the runtime cosh overflows above 710.4758600739439 in magnitude, so this must fail, and only above 710

log-finite-at-nonneg.why: real_log_finite with 0 <= x in place of 0 < x: log of zero is -inf, so this must fail, and only at zero

log-as-stated-until-2026-09-14.why: real_log_rounds as stated until 2026-09-14, with bound u; restated that day to 2u from this measurement, which found it false at inputs whose log lies just above a power of two (x = e^(±2^j)); kept so the run keeps showing it fails

abs-eps-zero-read-on-sin.why: the real_abs_eps_eq_zero row's exactness check pointed at the runtime sin, which rounds: it must see a nonzero error
